{{short description|All magnetic phenomena have analogous electric phenomena and vice versa}}
{{Distinguish|text = electric–magnetic duality, knows also as [[Montonen–Olive duality]]}}
{{sources exist|date=February 2025}}

In [[physics]], the '''electromagnetic dual''' concept is based on the idea that, in the static case, [[electromagnetism]] has two separate facets: [[electric field]]s and [[magnetic field]]s.<ref name="y959">{{cite book | last=Yang | first=Yisong | title=Mathematical Physics with Differential Equations | publisher=Oxford University Press | date=2023 | isbn=978-0-19-287261-6 | url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Mathematical_Physics_with_Differential_E/fZrMEAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Duality+(electricity+and+magnetism)&pg=PA61&printsec=frontcover | access-date=2025-07-25 | page=61}}</ref><ref name="e513">{{cite web | title=Electric–Magnetic Duality and Magnetic Monopoles | url=https://web2.ph.utexas.edu/~vadim/Classes/2024f-emt/duality.pdf |publisher=University of Texas at Austin |access-date=2025-07-25}}</ref>  Expressions in one of these will have a directly analogous, or dual, expression in the other.  The reason for this can ultimately be traced to [[special relativity]], where applying the [[Lorentz transformation]] to the electric field will transform it into a magnetic field. These are special cases of [[Duality (mathematics)|duality in mathematics]].

* The [[electric field]] ({{math|'''E'''}}) is the dual of the [[magnetic field]] ({{math|'''H'''}}).<ref name="l557">{{cite book | last=Krömer | first=Ralf | last2=Haffner | first2=Emmylou | title=Duality in 19th and 20th Century Mathematical Thinking | publisher=Springer Nature | date=2024-07-01 | isbn=978-3-031-59797-8 | url=https://www.google.co.uk/books/edition/Duality_in_19th_and_20th_Century_Mathema/CpYREQAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Duality+(electricity+and+magnetism)&pg=PA213&printsec=frontcover | access-date=2025-07-25 | page=213}}</ref>
* The [[electric displacement field]] ({{math|'''D'''}}) is the dual of the [[magnetic flux density]] ({{math|'''B'''}}).<ref name="l557"/>
* [[Faraday's law of induction]] is the dual of [[Ampère's circuital law]].
* [[Gauss's law]] for electric field is the dual of [[Gauss's law for magnetism]].
* The [[electric potential]] is the dual of the [[Magnetic scalar potential|magnetic potential]].
* [[Permittivity]] is the dual of [[Permeability (electromagnetism)|permeability]].
* [[Electrostriction]] is the dual of [[magnetostriction]].
* [[Piezoelectricity]] is the dual of [[piezomagnetism]].
* [[Ferroelectricity]] is the dual of [[ferromagnetism]].
* An [[electrostatic motor]]  is the dual of a [[electric motor|magnetic motor]];
* [[Electret]]s are the dual of [[magnet|permanent magnets]];
* The [[Faraday effect]] is the dual of the [[Kerr effect]];
* The [[Zeeman effect]] is the dual of the [[Stark effect]];
* The hypothetical [[magnetic monopole]] is the dual of [[electric charge]].

Additionally, in a sense different from the dualities above:
* The [[Aharonov–Casher effect]] is the dual to the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]].
In the usual sense of electromagnetic duality, the (unobserved) dual of the Aharonov-Bohm effect would be the phase acquired by a hypothetical magnetic monopole traveling through electric field. In contrast, the [[Aharonov–Casher effect]] is for a magnetic dipole (moment) in electric field, and its dual in the usual sense is for an electric dipole in magnetic field, which is distinct from the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]].
